issues.description: The only documented IRS access terms are historical: access was limited to two years, the contract required purge after the related project, and a petition to retain data was contemplated. The historical note describes then-current continuation on related projects, but present 2026 retention, user grant and authorized execution route are unknown; do not presume these inputs remain available.

The text starts with transformations on already-loaded IRS form-family datasets and uses abstract [file...] placeholders for form and master files. The datasheet says some raw-to-Stata preprocessing occurred before Stata and some confidential steps are redacted. Exact imports, input schemas, placeholder-to-dataset identities and secure processing setup are not supplied.

The supplied code consumes audit change data.dta twice and naics_3_fixed_effects.dta once, but this text has no producer for either handoff. The Table 6 merge file must supply naics_3 and fe and is followed by reads of med_assets, med_sales and perc_public; its schema, path and production order remain unresolved.

The complete text has unresolved variable contracts: the Form 1065 mapping creates dateincorporated but the age block consumes dateincorporated_new; Table 2 consumes match/winsor/owner-category fields such as gaap_aud_match, p1_gaap_match, audit_match, wtot_income_new_mil, wowner and owner_eq_1 without a producer in this file. These may be supplied by an undocumented input, so confirm the producer/schema rather than inventing aliases or transformations.

Table 6 requires prepared comp.dta and uses year separately from fyear for de-duplication/lags. The exact raw-to-prepared `year` mapping is not supplied. The branch expects count2, comp and ratio fields at collapse but does not define them; it does construct lev, btm, mtb, roa, pm, ppe_ratio, growth and other core ratios from raw Compustat fields. It also emits roa_sd_win in the first collapse but consumes roa_sd in the second. The locally readable COMP.FUNDA candidate does not establish the prepared-file mapping, missing aliases or required history, so the route remains unverified for those reasons.

The Stata code is stored in a TXT document and contains Windows-specific roots for three inputs and temporary outputs. Preparing a working .do copy and converting all affected paths to a consistent relative execution directory is routine setup. The separate [file...] identities, absent inputs and producers remain unresolved under the other issues.

The supplied text opens `audit change data.dta` with `clear` at line 745 and drops `f1120` at line 749. Later A3–A9 code consumes main IRS analysis state such as `paper`, `p1_*`, `f1120` and the state variables, but the source contains no subsequent `use`, `restore` or `preserve` command. The named `[masterfile2]` save is at line 172, before the paper/e-filer classification begins at line 177, and is not established as the required analysis snapshot. The exact post-main-analysis file, schema and reload point remain unknown. A10/A11 refer back to Tables 7/8 rather than supplying independent analysis code.

The Stata source contains 20 legacy `table ..., c(...)` calls. A self-written two-row Stata 18 probe returns rc 198 with the default command version (`option contents() not allowed since Stata 17`); the same one-way and Table 4-style two-way calls return rc 0 under the built-in `version 16:` prefix. A minimal supported source-preparation edit is available for the calls.
